equity.level_reason: Race/ethnicity, education, income and insurance only describe cases and respondents. MSM is used as a sexual-transmission risk group, so the side-by-side MSM rate is not read as a sexual-orientation contrast.

level_alternative.reason: The article mentions gay neighborhoods, the gay community and sexual orientation data; read as SOGI, the side-by-side MSM vs other-group rates are group-specific results, capped at 2 with no computed contrast.

equity.equity_measurement: MSM status is self-reported and unknown for 31% of male cases; the MSM rate denominator comes from the city HIV/AIDS epidemiology report and is compared with all other groups combined. SES describes only 64 male interview respondents.

notes: An outbreak report with counts, percentages, a rate comparison of MSM with other groups, and a PFGE pattern comparison, with no p-values or models. The MSM rate contrast is read as a transmission category rather than sexual orientation, so equity is level 1, and a level 2 reading is given as the alternative. The PFGE comparison is the only laboratory method recorded because it produces the compared proportions. [review] Sex is a descriptor of cases rather than a population restriction; the case definition restricts only by county and age. The PFGE comparison is retained as a procedure because it produces the compared pattern-sharing proportions.
view_issues: The case period is June--December 2000 in one sentence and May--December 2000 in another, and the age threshold is over 15 years in the footnote but over 18 years for interviews.
